 Matthew Farwell convicted of killing Sandra Birchmore and unborn child in Massachusetts murder trial
 By
 Neal Riley , 
 Neal Riley 
 Digital Producer, CBS Boston 
 Neal J. Riley is a digital producer for CBS Boston. He has been with WBZ-TV since 2014. His work has appeared in The Boston Globe and The San Francisco Chronicle. Neal is a graduate of Boston University.
 Read Full Bio 
 Neal Riley , 
 Kristina Rex 
 Kristina Rex 
 Reporter, CBS Boston 
 Kristina Rex is a reporter for WBZ-TV News.
 Read Full Bio 
 Kristina Rex 
 Updated on: November 10, 2026 / 2:24 PM EST 
 / CBS Boston
 Add CBS News on Google 
 A jury has found former Stoughton, Massachusetts, police officer  Matthew Farwell  guilty of killing Sandra Birchmore and her unborn child. The verdict was read in federal court in South Boston Tuesday afternoon.
 Farwell was charged with killing a witness or victim and causing the death of an unborn child. He pleaded not guilty. The jury had previously said in a note on Monday that it was "in a deadlock." 
 There were gasps from Birchmore's family as the verdict was read aloud in court.
 Farwell faces a mandatory sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole. Sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 3, 2027. The Department of Justice could have pursued the death penalty against Farwell, but decided last year it would not.  
 Jurors heard from 50 witnesses over four weeks of testimony. To convict Farwell on the charge of killing a witness or victim, jurors had to find find that he not only killed Birchmore, but that he did so to prevent her from reporting his crimes to federal authorities.  
 "Despite Mr. Farwell's attempt to silence Sandra Birchmore, today her story is told," U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Leah Foley said in a statement. "The mountain of evidence against Matthew Farwell uncloaked his chilling and diabolical actions and lies. He now faces life in federal prison. Justice has indeed been served."
 Farwell and Birchmore met when she was a 13-year-old cadet in the Stoughton Police Department's youth explorers program. Prosecutors say Farwell began a sexual relationship with her when she was just 15. 
 The 23-year-old Birchmore was found dead in her Canton apartment with a strap hanging around her neck in February 2021. Her death was initially ruled a suicide. But more than three years later, Farwell was arrested and the medical examiner changed Birchmore's manner of death to "undetermined."
 Prosecutors made the case that Farwell strangled Birchmore, who was pregnant with what she believed was his child, and then staged her death to look like a suicide in order to cover up their years-long affair. The defense said Birchmore had a history of mental health problems and committed suicide because Farwell told her he was not the father and the relationship was over. 
 Barbara Wright, Birchmore's cousin, said she was feeling a mixture of sadness, happiness and relief.
 "It's been almost six years since we lost Sandra and let's not forget her baby boy," she said outside court. "We finally got justice. We've been fighting long and hard for her. And she deserves it. She's waited a long time."  
 This is a breaking news story that will be updated as more information is available.
